BC_PROGRAM_UUID.description: Server-side Bugcrowd program-scope predicate forwarded as the filter[program][]=<uuid> query parameter on GET /submissions. Optional; empty / blank walks the entire token's program scope (the typical operational mode for a single-program identity). Comma-separated uuids / handles are split and trimmed, then forwarded as multiple filter[program][]=<uuid> entries so a single agent can pull submissions from several programs in one run (e.g. '11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555,acme-prod,acme-mobile'). Bugcrowd accepts either the program's uuid or its slug (handle); the operator's token scope still applies. Whitespace is trimmed around each entry.

BC_STATE.description: Server-side Bugcrowd submission-state filter (CSV: 'new' / 'triaged' / 'unresolved' / 'resolved' / 'duplicate' / 'not-reproducible' / 'not-applicable' / 'out-of-scope' / 'informational' / 'needs-reproduction' / 'spam'). Forwarded as a single comma-joined filter[state][]=<csv> query parameter (Bugcrowd accepts both the comma-joined form and one entry per state but the joined form avoids URL ballooning when the operator supplies many states). Operator-friendly aliases are normalised ('open' -> 'unresolved', 'nr' -> 'not-reproducible', 'na' / 'not_applicable' / 'notapplicable' -> 'not-applicable', 'oos' / 'out_of_scope' / 'outofscope' -> 'out-of-scope', 'dup' -> 'duplicate', 'info' -> 'informational', 'closed' / 'fixed' -> 'resolved', 'needs-info' -> 'needs-reproduction'). Blank / missing walks every state (the typical operational mode for first-time imports). Unknown / unparseable entries are dropped silently rather than crashing the run.

BC_MIN_PRIORITY.description: Optional Bugcrowd priority floor (integer 1..5, where 1 is most critical and 5 is least); submissions whose priority is numerically greater than the floor (less severe) are dropped client-side after the fetch. Bugcrowd's priority ladder maps to Faraday severities as P1 -> 'critical', P2 -> 'high', P3 -> 'medium', P4 -> 'low', P5 -> 'info'. Accepts integer / float / 'P<N>' scalar inputs ('P1' / '1' / '1.0' all parse the same). Closed / Resolved / Duplicate / Not-Reproducible / Not-Applicable / Out-Of-Scope / Informational / Spam submissions are floored to 'info' severity regardless of the published priority (preserved via an explicit BC-State pivot). Blank / missing / unparseable values keep every record (the typical operational mode for first-time imports).

name: bugcrowd
title: Bugcrowd
description: Bugcrowd crowd-sourced bug-bounty submission importer. Pulls validated submissions from the Bugcrowd REST API and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Bugcrowd is a crowd-sourced security platform — external researchers submit vulnerability reports against a program's scope and the program triages, validates, prioritises, and pays out on the resulting findings. This executor surfaces validated submissions under the operator's existing Faraday workspace so the external bug-bounty pipeline joins the dispatcher's internal scanner output. Endpoints used: GET https://api.bugcrowd.com/submissions?filter[program][]=<uuid>&filter[state][]=<csv>&page[offset]=N&page[limit]=M (paginated bug-bounty submission feed; canonical envelope is JSON:API {'data': [{'id': '...', 'type': 'submission', 'attributes': {...}, 'relationships': {...}}], 'meta': {'total_hits': N}, 'links': {'next': '...', 'prev': '...'}} with each record's attributes carrying title, description / vulnerability_information, state (new / triaged / unresolved / resolved / duplicate / not-reproducible / not-applicable / out-of-scope / informational / needs-reproduction / spam — Bugcrowd's published state machine), substate, priority (integer 1..5 — Bugcrowd's P1..P5 ladder where P1 is most critical and P5 is least), cvss_vector / cvss_score, vrt_id (Bugcrowd's Vulnerability Rating Taxonomy id), bug_url (URL / asset the researcher targeted), cve (attributed CVE strings), created_at / submitted_at / triaged_at / resolved_at / disclosed_at / last_updated_at, monetary_reward / reward_currency; relationships carries pointers to program (uuid + handle), researcher (username), target (scoped asset), and vrt (canonical issue-type ontology with CWE mapping)). Auth: Bugcrowd's REST surface uses a single long-lived API token in the Authorization: Token <token> header (no username — the token alone is the identity). The dispatcher locks the API version with the Accept: application/vnd.bugcrowd.v4+json header so later API breaking changes do not silently warp the ingest shape. BC_HOST is an env-only override (defaults to https://api.bugcrowd.com); whitespace is trimmed and https:// is added when the operator pasted in a bare FQDN. Pagination is offset-based via JSON:API's page[offset]=N + page[limit]=M (Bugcrowd caps page[limit] at 100); walks until len(records) < page_size or the env-only BC_PAGES knob is reached (default 10, clamped to [1, 100]). 401 short-circuits the whole executor (credentials are wrong); 403 / 429 / 5xx stop pagination and return what we have. Each Bugcrowd submission becomes one Faraday host with host.ip set to the 0.0.0.0 sentinel (bug-bounty submissions are keyed on a URL / asset path rather than an IP); the submission title and the bug_url URL land on host.hostnames; the submission itself becomes one Faraday vulnerability with the [BUG-BOUNTY] engine prefix so external researcher reports land alongside the other crowd-sourced feeds. Severity bucketing: Bugcrowd's P1..P5 ladder maps to Faraday's critical / high / medium / low / info ladder (P1 -> critical, P2 -> high, P3 -> medium, P4 -> low, P5 -> info); integer / 'P<N>' scalar inputs are accepted. Closed / Resolved / Duplicate / Not-Reproducible / Not-Applicable / Out-Of-Scope / Informational / Spam submissions are floored to 'info' regardless of the published priority (preserved via an explicit BC-State pivot). Unparseable / missing priority defaults to 'info'. Status is always 'open' so the operator's remediation workflow takes over; the closed state is preserved via the info-severity floor + the BC-State pivot. Refs include explicit BC-SubmissionID / BC-Program / BC-Researcher / BC-State / BC-Substate / BC-Priority / BC-CreatedAt / BC-SubmittedAt / BC-TriagedAt / BC-ResolvedAt / BC-DisclosedAt / BC-UpdatedAt / BC-Reward / BC-Currency / BC-Source / BC-BugURL / BC-CVSSVector / BC-CVSSScore / BC-VRT pivots, plus the canonical https://bugcrowd.com/<program> / https://bugcrowd.com/<researcher> / https://tracker.bugcrowd.com/submissions/<id> / https://bugcrowd.com/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy permalinks and the canonical NVD CVE + MITRE CWE permalinks for any CVE / CWE ids surfaced in the cve / vrt / description / title fields. Tags: [bugcrowd, pentest-platforms, submission].
